name: Asakusa
description: Asakusa and the Skytree from open data, lit by the real sun: Senso-ji, the Kaminarimon's lantern, Nakamise, the Sumida and its water bus, and Tokyo Skytree across the river.

imagery.attribution: Geospatial Information Authority of Japan (GSI) seamless aerial photographs (GSI terms of use, source attribution)

terrain.attribution: GSI Fundamental Geospatial Data DEM5A, 5 m airborne laser survey bare earth (GSI terms of use); 10 m DEM where 5A is absent

terrain_check.name: GSI elevation API (1 m laser DEM where flown, otherwise DEM5)

plateau.attribution: MLIT Project PLATEAU Tokyo 23 wards LOD2 building models (CC BY 4.0), as vector tiles by indigo-lab (MIT)

seawall.note: The rivers' and the bay's revetments and the castle moats: granite blocks and concrete.

trees.note: Species are not mapped. Elms stand for the zelkovas (keyaki) and the ginkgos of Senso-ji's precinct, plane trees for the street trees of Edo-dori and the Sumida's banks. A guess, not a survey.

tour.title: Asakusa, from open data
tour.text: {buildings} buildings. {share:plateau}% of the footprint area stands at a height Project PLATEAU surveyed, on GSI's 5 m laser-scanned bare earth.

tour.title: Senso-ji
tour.text: The approach runs north from the Kaminarimon, between Nakamise's shops, through the Hozomon to the main hall, with the five-storey pagoda to its left. The gates, pagoda and hall are built to their published sizes: the pagoda {landmark:sensoji.pagoda.top_m} m to the tip of its finial.

tour.title: Tokyo Skytree
tour.text: 634 m: a triangle 68 m a side at the foot, a circle by 320 m. The Tembo Deck is at 350 m, the Galleria at 450 m. After dark it is lit, one night in Iki's blue, the next in Miyabi's purple.

tour.title: Where the heights come from
tour.text: Blue: surveyed height (PLATEAU or OpenStreetMap). Orange: floor count. Green: estimated. Grey: a typical height for its kind.

sources.landmarks: Senso-ji's Kaminarimon (11.7 m; the lantern 3.9 m, 3.3 m across, about 700 kg), Hozomon (21.7 m; the 小舟町 lantern 3.75 m; the sandals 4.5 m), five-storey pagoda (53.32 m) and main hall (29.4 m) from Senso-ji and OpenStreetMap, placed on OpenStreetMap's footprints; Tokyo Skytree from Tobu Tower Skytree (634 m; a 68 m triangle at the foot; Tembo Deck 350 m, Tembo Galleria 450 m; Iki and Miyabi lighting); the Asahi Flamme d'Or (Philippe Starck, 1989) from photographs. Proportions of roofs and lattices are approximations.
sources.fonts: Lanterns and plaques drawn with Google Fonts under the SIL Open Font License: Yuji Syuku, Shippori Mincho

game.title: Asakusa on Foot
game.blurb: Walk the real Asakusa, rebuilt from open data and lit by the real sun: the Kaminarimon's lantern, Nakamise, Senso-ji, the water bus on the Sumida, and the lift up Tokyo Skytree to the Tembo Deck, 350 m up.

wharves.terminal: 浅草二天門(水上バス乗り場)

ferry_style.note: The shared harbour ferry stands in for the Sumida's water buses; the white and navy are approximate.

ferries.route: Sumida River Line 隅田川ライン

game.ferry_note: Piers are from OpenStreetMap via Overture. The route runs between the piers on this map; the timetable is not real. Tokyo Cruise and the Tokyo Mizube Line run on to Hinode, Hamarikyu and Odaiba from here.

areas.name: 浅草
areas.note: The Kaminarimon and Nakamise: where a game sends you to buy a gift

npcs.name: Sota 颯太
idle: A ride round Asakusa? Thirty minutes, and I'll tell you which shop has the best ningyo-yaki.
Rickshaws came back to Asakusa in the 1990s. The legs remember the old streets. {sun_line}

npcs.name: Fumiko 文子
idle: 人形焼, ningyo-yaki: sponge cake with red bean, in the shape of the pagoda and the lantern. Fresh, still warm.
Eat by the shop, please. Walking and eating on Nakamise isn't done.

npcs.name: Kosuke 浩介
idle: Kannon was found in the river in 628, and the temple grew round her. Tokyo's oldest.
At New Year three million people come through the Kaminarimon. Today is quiet. {time}.

npcs.name: Captain Hiroshi 浩
idle: Up the Sumida and down to the bay. The bridges are the best part: every one a different colour.
The golden thing over the river? Asahi's flame. Everyone calls it something else.

npcs.name: Rina 里奈
idle: Six hundred metres a minute: fifty seconds to the Tembo Deck. Your ears will pop.
634 m: 武蔵, Musashi, the old name of this province. The height was chosen for the pun.

npcs.name: Kei 慶
idle: A book sent me here, can you believe it. Shitamachi, the old low city.
I drew 凶 at the fortune box. Tied it on the rack. Trying again tomorrow.

quests.title: The Thunder Gate
talk: いらっしゃい! First time in Asakusa? This is the Kaminarimon, the Thunder Gate. Look up: the lantern weighs about 700 kg.
This is the real Asakusa, rebuilt from open data: {buildings} buildings, {share:plateau}% of the footprint area at heights Project PLATEAU surveyed.
Walk up Nakamise to the temple. Fumiko's shop is halfway, on the right. WASD to walk, Shift to run, E to talk.

steps.text: Look up at the Kaminarimon's lantern

quests.title: Nakamise
talk: Nakamise: about ninety shops on 250 m, some since Edo. Rice crackers, fans, wigs for festivals, ningyo-yaki.
Through the Hozomon, with its big 小舟町 lantern, and you're at the hall. Kosuke helps at the incense burner.

steps.text: Talk to Kosuke in front of the main hall

quests.title: Your fortune
talk: Draw an omikuji: shake the box, read the number, open that drawer. Senso-ji's are honest; about three in ten are 凶.
The pagoda beside us is 53 m to the top of its finial, rebuilt in 1973. The hall in 1958: both burned in the 1945 air raids.

steps.text: Talk to Kei by the pagoda

quests.title: Down the Sumida
talk: The water bus leaves from here. Ride it to Komagatabashi and back and you'll see why people paint this river.
Across the water: Asahi's black hall with the golden flame, and the Skytree behind it.

steps.text: Find Rina at the foot of the Skytree

quests.title: Tembo Deck
talk: The lift is by the door: E to call it. Tembo Deck at 350 m, then the Galleria at 450 m if you're brave.
On a clear winter day you can see Mt Fuji from up there. {sun_line}

steps.text: Look out from the Tembo Deck
